journey:beckmann-descent-from-the-cross.l: The Museum of Modern Art, New York, USA

x.summary: Painted after Beckmann suffered a breakdown while serving as a medical orderly in the First World War, this work shows Christ's oversized, rigid body being lowered from the cross. The arms remain stretched out as though still nailed, and the distorted, crowded figures recall German late medieval and Renaissance altarpieces. It is one of the most searing images of the dead Christ to come out of the Great War, where the suffering of Christ and the suffering of a generation are one.
facts: Beckmann looked back to German painters such as Matthias Grünewald and Hans Holbein, borrowing their stark, angular figures to express the horror he had witnessed as a medical orderly.
Christ's body is pale, bruised and stiff with rigor mortis, and his arms remain locked in the shape of the cross even after being taken down; a darkened sun hangs at the upper left.
In 1937 the Nazis condemned Beckmann as a 'degenerate' artist; he left Germany the day after Hitler's speech opening the Great German Art Exhibition and never returned.
